routes.name: Visa-free short stay (Schengen)
routes.summary: Nationals of visa-exempt countries can visit without a visa for short stays. Switzerland is in Schengen, so the usual limit is 90 days in any 180 days. Check the official nationality list.

other: I could not open the official visa-exempt list or a page stating the 90/180 rule, so the exact country list and day limit need checking on the SEM nationality list linked in the sources.

routes.name: Schengen C visa (short stay)
routes.summary: Citizens of countries on the visa list need a Schengen C visa for short stays. Apply through a Swiss representation abroad. The SEM itself does not issue visas.

other: Travel document valid at least 3 months after you plan to leave the Schengen area
Show the purpose and conditions of your stay and enough funds
No Schengen Information System entry refusal and no threat to public order, security, health or international relations
Check the official nationality list to see if your passport needs a visa
A valid residence permit from another Schengen country can replace the visa

steps: Check the nationality list to see if you need a visa
Apply through the Swiss representation abroad or the online portal
Attend the appointment with your documents

routes.name: ETIAS travel authorization (not live yet)
routes.summary: ETIAS is a planned EU travel authorization for visa-exempt travelers to Schengen countries, including Switzerland. Applications are not open yet.

other: No start date has been set. The EU will announce it a few months ahead.
Some travelers are exempt from the fee.

routes.name: EU/EFTA free movement (AFMP)
routes.summary: EU and EFTA citizens can enter, live and work in Switzerland under the free movement agreement. Stays over 3 months need registration with the commune and a residence permit.

other: UK nationals have been treated like non-EU/EFTA nationals, including quotas, since 1 January 2021. Those with rights from before 2021 may keep them under special provisions.

routes.name: EU/EFTA employee permit (L or B)
routes.summary: For EU/EFTA citizens with a job. Up to 3 months with a Swiss employer needs no permit, just a notification by the employer. Longer jobs need a permit from your commune.

other: Apply to your commune before starting, with ID or passport and proof of employment
Employer notifies the work at least one day before for jobs up to 3 months
